note: First real change since Week 1 kicked off: Demarcus Robinson is upgraded from yesterday's AVOID to PURSUE off a confirmed Thursday line (2 catches on 3 targets, 50 yards, a 39-yard TD in San Francisco's 27-7 win) -- one game of live production in a receiver room still down Christian Kirk and Ricky Pearsall, with De'Zhaun Stribling banged up too. Drop candidate is Mike Washington, not Quentin Johnston -- Ashton Jeanty cleared Thursday's practice report with no designation, so Washington is back to a pure zero-touch handcuff. Two Saturday-into-Sunday depth-chart items close off speculative adds rather than open them: Arizona's own Week 1 depth chart names Tyler Allgeier RB1 over Jeremiyah Love, burying Bam Knight at RB3 with no path; and Malik Davis's season-ending hip surgery hands Dallas' RB3 job to Emari Demercado, but Javonte Williams remains the unambiguous starter, so there's no fantasy-relevant opportunity behind him. Kyle Williams (NE) is added as a watch-only stash -- fresh reporting has him third on the Patriots' depth chart behind Romeo Doubs, not the presumptive A.J.-Brown-injury beneficiary the Sept 11 buzz implied. Ian Thomas (LV) is a speculative TE3 watch while Brock Bowers is out (Raiders OC Janocko: 'it's a 17-game season'), but there's no clean drop to justify a bid this week. Darren Waller and Tre Tucker (yesterday's WATCH entries) are unchanged -- Carolina and Las Vegas haven't played yet today, revisit after kickoff.

targets.why: Listed as San Francisco's starting WR3 alongside Deebo Samuel and Mike Evans with Christian Kirk (IR) and Ricky Pearsall (season-ending) both out, then backed it up Thursday: 2 catches on 3 targets for 50 yards and a 39-yard touchdown from Brock Purdy in a 27-7 win over the Rams (NBC Sports, FanDuel Research, Sept. 10).
targets.asset: recent-trend (wk 1) -- 2/3 targets, 50 yds, 1 TD in San Francisco's opener; a WR3/4 role in a thinned, pass-heavy receiver room rather than a defined every-week share
targets.my_team_impact: Doesn't crack your starting lineup over Pickens/Egbuka, but is a clear upgrade on Mike Washington's zero-touch RB stash for your final bench spot -- a real catch-and-explosive-play role behind two ahead-of-him starters, on the NFL's most efficient Week 1 offense so far (27 points).
targets.confidence_why: One game of real production, but it's a single sample in a three-wideout room where the coaching staff hasn't named a fixed target hierarchy behind Samuel and Evans.
targets.competition: Evans is StoneBone69's and Samuel is ENOTS's, so two rivals are exposed to this offense but neither has an acute WR hole that would push them to bid on SF's WR3.
targets.bid: 2 dollars -- no competing interest, no reason to bid past the routine-uncontested floor
targets.drop: Mike Washington -- Jeanty cleared Thursday's report with no designation, so Washington is back to a pure zero-touch handcuff with no Week 1 path.

targets.why: CORRECTION to the Sept 11 item's 'breakout buzz' framing: fresh Week 1 outlook reporting (RotoBaller, Boston.com) has Williams third on New England's depth chart behind Romeo Doubs, not the direct A.J. Brown-injury beneficiary implied earlier, with Hunter Henry also competing for targets.
targets.asset: role-based -- WR3 on a run-first-questionable offense; a strong preseason (6-166-3) hasn't yet translated to a named Week 1 role
targets.my_team_impact: You already roster the direct beneficiary of the Brown injury (Kayshon Boutte's own team, not this one) -- Williams would be a pure speculative stash, not a Week 1 lineup piece, and there's no bench spot to spare for a WR3 on someone else's depth chart.
targets.confidence_why: Preseason flash hasn't converted to a confirmed target share; Doubs sits ahead of him on the depth chart into Week 1.
targets.competition: No HBGBs roster currently holds a Patriots pass-catcher.
targets.bid: n/a -- watch only, no roster space to justify a bid this week

targets.why: Raiders OC Andrew Janocko has flagged expanded 12-personnel snaps for Thomas while Brock Bowers is out for the opener (meniscus trim) and framed the absence in multi-week terms ('it's a 17-game season, we have a 70-man roster' -- The Sporting Tribune, Sept. 10), with Michael Mayer starting in Bowers' place.
targets.asset: role-based -- expanded 12-personnel snaps, no confirmed target share of his own
targets.my_team_impact: Sam LaPorta and Jake Ferguson both hold real starting TE value already; Thomas would be a pure speculative 3rd-TE stash with no bench room to open for him.
targets.confidence_why: Snap-count language from the OC, not a target-share report -- Mayer, not Thomas, is the confirmed Week 1 beneficiary of Bowers' absence.
targets.competition: Mayer himself is rostered (Stipe); no rival roster is chasing Thomas specifically.

targets.why: Moves up to Dallas' RB2 after Malik Davis's Friday hip injury and Saturday season-ending surgery (ESPN, Sept. 11), but Javonte Williams remains the unambiguous starter with no snap-share erosion reported.
targets.asset: handcuff-only -- zero third-down or change-of-pace role reported
targets.my_team_impact: You already roster five running backs; a zero-touch handcuff to a healthy starter you don't own isn't worth the spot.
targets.confidence_why: Handcuff value only matters if Javonte Williams gets hurt, and even then it's someone else's roster (mfkr) that would care.
targets.competition: Javonte Williams is mfkr's; Demercado's value is specific to that roster, not yours.

targets.why: Arizona's own Week 1 depth chart names Tyler Allgeier RB1 and Jeremiyah Love RB2, with Knight third and no reported role even if Love's ankle limits him (Yahoo Sports, Sept. 8).
targets.asset: buried depth -- no path to touches reported
targets.my_team_impact: No fit -- you don't roster either back ahead of him, and a third-string RB on a run-committee offense isn't a speculative add worth a bench spot.
targets.confidence_why: Named depth chart with two backs ahead of him closes this off, not just a hunch.
targets.competition: Allgeier is ENOTS's, Love is mfkr's -- Knight's value is speculative even for those two rosters.
